headline: Africa: Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Africa: Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter.
- Western Russia: Two injured, buildings destroyed and damaged in Russian attack on Odesa Oblast – photos, video.
- South Asia: Seeing red in Iran.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Under threat of air strikes, US looks to bolster base infrastructure with 3D printing.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Under threat of air strikes, US looks to bolster base infrastructure with 3D printing.
U.S. Air Force officials conceded that troop housing at Middle East bases was "never designed for the threat environment now arriving overhead."
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Amid Iran conflict, ‘non-hostile’ deaths of 2 US airmen raise overseas toll.
Two U.S. airmen supporting operations against Iran died last week in "non-hostile" incidents, raising the death toll to 23 since the war began.
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: The Pentagon needs more ammo for the Iran war. Small communities are paying the price..
From polluted waterways to repeated safety violations, the Army’s aging ammunition factories have left a troubling legacy, The War Horse reports.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘Kevin Smith killed Taneka Gardner’ - Pathways murder accused continues to reject murder statement.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 19 hours ago: ‘Kevin Smith killed Taneka Gardner’ - Pathways murder accused continues to reject murder statement.
Murder accused Andre Ruddock has denied fabricating a story that a detective constable had instructed him to take the blame for killing Taneka Gardner on behalf of late church leader Kevin Smith. Ruddock, who is on trial for Gardner’s murder in the Home Circuit Court, maintained under cross-examination on Tuesday that he was telling the truth. “I am suggesting to you that on October 17, 2021, you, Andre Ruddock, cut the throat of Taneka Gardner,” lead prosecutor LaToya Bernard said. “Not true. Kevin Smith killed Taneka Gardner,” Ruddock answered.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: ‘It was a hunt’: Outrage over an attack on trans women in Palermo.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 21 hours ago: ‘It was a hunt’: Outrage over an attack on trans women in Palermo.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Two injured, buildings destroyed and damaged in Russian attack on Odesa Oblast – photos, video.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Two injured, buildings destroyed and damaged in Russian attack on Odesa Oblast – photos, video.
State Emergency Service has confirmed two injuries after Russian strikes destroyed a footwear warehouse and damaged a postal depot in Odesa Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Forty people confirmed killed in Russian aerial bomb attack on school in Komyshuvakha – photos, video.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says 40 people have been confirmed killed in the Russian strike, while more than 30 may still be trapped under the rubble.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Military video shows drone striking state-of-the-art US$45m Russian Buk-M3 system.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps has released a video showing a strike drone hitting a state-of-the-art Russian Buk-M3 anti-aircraft missile system worth US$45 million.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian forces kill man in Antonivka, Kherson Oblast, in drone attack.
A resident of the settlement of Antonivka in Kherson Oblast has been killed in a Russian drone attack on the afternoon of 4 November.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle to visit EU Parliament.
- Politico Europe, 8 hours ago: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle to visit EU Parliament.
Couple will be in Brussels to talk about online child safety.
- Politico Europe, 11 hours ago: Fridge hacks also hit French blood banks.
The incident appears to be connected to a recent wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators across Europe.
- Balkan Insight, 15 hours ago: Kosovo Identifies Three More Wartime Missing Persons.
Three Kosovo Albanian intellectuals who were forcibly disappeared by Serbian forces in April 1999 have been identified in a mass grave in the north of Kosovo.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Ukraine: Police footage captures Russian strike on Komyshuvakha shelter.
Bodycam footage from a police officer killed in the attack captures the moments before a Russian bomb strikes a shelter in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 37 people.
- Africanews, 15 hours ago: Ukraine: 33 dead, over 50 missing after Russian bombing in Zaporizhzhia.
Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region have killed 33 people, with more than 50 still missing, on Monday 2 November. Survivors and rescuers are being treated for severe injuries.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 16 hours ago: Sudan: 'This Is Not About Politics. This Is About People' - UN Warns of Impact of Deadly Drone Strikes in Sudan.
[UN News] Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN's top official in the country has warned.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Ethiopia: Death of Three, Injuries of 20 Kenyans Attributed to Ethiopia's Moyale Conflict.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A Kenyan woman was killed by a suspected stray bullet in the border town of Moyale on 2 November, bringing to three the reported number of Kenyans killed in conflict linked to ongoing clashes in Moyale of neighbouring Ethiopia, according to Kenyan media reports.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran's political, religious leaders shift stance to support nuclear weapons as war looms - report.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Iran's political, religious leaders shift stance to support nuclear weapons as war looms - report.
In past decades, Iranian officials have publicly endorsed the fatwa issued by supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei forbidding the development and use of nuclear weapons.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 20 hours ago: Malawi: Mukhito Vows Crackdown On Digital Deception - Freedom of Expression Does Not Cover Fraud.
[Nyasa Times] A man accused of faking official government statements has been arrested, and the Homeland Security Minister has used the case to warn Malawians about the dangers of artificial intelligence and social media being used to spread lies.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 20 hours ago: Malawi: Pathologist Says Chilima Died Instantly, Rejects Hijack Claims Before Parliament.
[Nyasa Times] A pathologist who examined the bodies of former vice-president Saulos Chilima and seven others killed in the June 10, 2024 plane crash has told Parliament that the victims died instantly and that the evidence does not support claims of a hijacking.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Seeing red in Iran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Seeing red in Iran.
IN the run-up to yesterday’s US mid-term elections, it became obvious that, almost four decades after the Cold War ended, the ‘spectre of communism’ Marx and Engels identified in the 19th century still haunts Western consciousness. Islamophobia might have been the most prominent weapon, but it was accompanied by diatribes against Marxists and communists, invariably directed against people who are neither. For good measure, some of them are simultaneously derided as Islamist jihadists.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Israel president urges compromise after divisive election.
Israel’s president on Wednesday opened talks on forming a new government with a call for compromise, saying neither side had won divisive elections, as he also condemned “racist” rhetoric against Arab parties that made sharp gains. More than a week after Israel’s first election since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 19 hours ago: Fazl hints at launching street agitation.
MANSEHRA: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman said here on Tuesday that his party would never allow the government to plunder the natural resources and deprive people of their democratic rights in the country. “The government wants to divide the nation and create conflict to plunder natural resources. We will never allow it to undermine democracy, politics and rights of people. JUI-F stands firm against such anti-people policies and actions,” he told a workers convention, hinting at launching a street agitation.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: Pakistan's Maliha Ali topples Russia's Drozdova at MMA world championships.
Russia arrived at the IMMAF World Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia, with more than 60 athletes, government backing and one of the best-funded programmes in the sport. On Tuesday, a 24-year-old from Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan, beat one of them. Maliha Ali defeated Veronika Drozdova, a two-time European champion and, at 19, by split decision in their featherweight (65.8kg) bout at the world championships of amateur mixed martial arts.

Under the banner “Enough is Enough”, 11 high school and university student associations marched from Copenhagen’s City Hall Square to parliament over the proposed cuts to free up funds for defence spending.
